blocks.text: I’ve got enough to answer the “why” now. The short version is that Browser MCP is carrying real OS/browser lifecycle state, while our normal app checks are mostly pure build/test checks; stale daemon/profile state can survive across agent sessions and make the …

Because Browser MCP is not just “run a screenshot tool.” It is a live chain: `agent -> provider MCP client -> unpeel-host __browser_mcp__ -> agent-browser CLI -> native daemon -> system Chrome -> target page` Any layer can be fine while the next one is wedged. …
